As of **October 2026**, the latest **publicly available Claude model is *Claude Opus 4.7*** [2], which launched in **early 2026** as Anthropic’s most capable consumer model at the time. Opus 4.7 improves on its predecessor with **multi-step reasoning** (breaking tasks into subtasks and running them in parallel) and maintains a **1 million-token context window** (in beta). The Sonnet branch was also updated to **Sonnet 4.6** (released February 2026) [1], which added full multimodality (text, voice, and image inputs/outputs) and advanced coding capabilities, though Opus remains the top tier.

ChatGPT’s latest is **ChatGPT Images 2.5** (released **September 8, 2026**) [4], with a **GPT-5 core** (not a distinct "GPT-6" yet). This version focuses on **image fidelity** (better editing without disturbing original elements) and **reference accuracy** for real-world objects. Unlike Claude, ChatGPT now includes **ads in the free tier** [6], but OpenAI insists they don’t influence responses.

---

The latest Claude model from Anthropic is **Claude Opus 4.7** [2], while the latest ChatGPT model is **GPT-5** [5].

## Model Comparison
**Claude Opus 4.7** is Anthropic's most capable publicly available model [2]. While the source material doesn't list every specific benchmark for 4.7, its predecessor, **Claude Opus 4.6**, established a high baseline with a **90.2% score on BigLaw Bench** [1]. 

The Claude 4.6 series introduced several architectural improvements relevant to your background:
*   **Context Window**: A **one million token context window** (currently in beta) [1].
*   **Reasoning**: Improved **multi-step reasoning** that decomposes complex tasks into subtasks and executes them in parallel [1].
*   **Multimodality**: Native support for text, voice dictation, and image inputs, with the ability to output **text artifacts, diagrams, and TTS audio** [1].

**GPT-5** is currently positioned as a model that excels at **writing and analysis** [5]. OpenAI's recent updates (specifically for the Images 2.5 generation) focus on **reference fidelity** and complex layout handling [4].

## Coding Verdict
I would use **Claude Sonnet 4.6** for coding.

answer_raw:
**Claude Opus 4.7** is the latest public model from Anthropic, launched **February 5, 2026**, with a **1-million-token context window** (beta), parallelized multi-step reasoning, and top-tier domain-specific scores like **90.2% on BigLaw Bench** (from Opus 4.6, no 4.7 benchmarks yet) [1][2]. It handles text, voice, and image inputs while outputting artifacts like diagrams and TTS audio.

**ChatGPT’s latest is Images 2.5 (Sep 8, 2026)**, a multimodal model focused on **image generation and editing**, not core coding or reasoning [4]. Its text backend—likely still **GPT-4.x**—isn’t updated in the sources; OpenAI’s GPT-5 isn’t mentioned as deployed [5], and its **core text model remains unconfirmed**. Images 2.5 excels at fidelity and layout but lacks the structured reasoning updates seen in Claude’s latest releases.

---
### **For coding**
**Claude Sonnet 4.6** (released **Feb 17, 2026**) is the **best pick**—it’s the **latest for coding tasks**, with a **full upgrade** across code handling, agent planning, and multimodal outputs [1]. Opus 4.7 is newer but lacks a coding-specific benchmark and targets broader reasoning workloads. Sonnet’s strengths include:
- **Parallel subtask execution** for complex scripts.
- **Native diagram/text artifact generation** for engineering tasks.
- **Multimodality** (voice + image inputs/outputs) if your workflow involves mixed media [1].

ChatGPT Images 2.5 won’t help with code—it’s specialized for visual output. Its text abilities are **untested for modern benchmarks** and likely lag behind Sonnet’s architecture. If you need **image generation alongside code**, Omni AI’s free app lets you toggle between models via a unified interface, though pricing/access depends on your setup [5].

---
### **Why this gap?**
The sources don’t name a **GPT-5 or GPT-6 release** in 2026—only the **Images 2.5** multimodal branch. OpenAI’s ad testing in free-tier ChatGPT also adds noise; Anthropic’s ad-free stance contrasts with that [6]. For verified specs, stick to Claude’s released benchmarks and focus on Sonnet 4.6 for coding, Opus 4.7 for general reasoning.
